title: Repeat a Word and Its Meaning Disappears
hook: Say one word over and over and something strange happens
summary: Repeat the same word again and again and its meaning briefly disappears. This is called semantic satiation.

text: Try saying this word over and over in your head.
apple apple apple apple apple apple
apple apple apple apple apple apple

panels.text: Huh? Apple doesn't feel like apple anymore

text: Suddenly the word sounds like a strange noise.

panels.mean: when repeating a word makes it lose its meaning for a moment

text: In 1962, at McGill University in Canada,
Leon Jakobovits James gave it this name in his PhD thesis.
Staring at one word for a long time without saying it does something similar.
It's that feeling when familiar letters suddenly look weird.
Luckily, it's only for a moment.
After a bit, the word gets its meaning back.
